title: Rabbi Yehoshua ben Kefosai

paragraphs: Rabbi Yehoshua ben Kefosai (or Kabsa, Kabsoy, Kofsai, Kefutzai).[^3]

His beginnings reach back to the generation of Rabban Gamliel and Rabbi Akiva. As in the Tosefta, Mikvaot, which relates an incident involving Rabban Gamliel and Onkelos the convert, Rabbi Yehoshua ben Kofsai said (in the Zuckermandel Tosefta: ben Kevusai): ‘I was with them, and Rabban Gamliel immersed only in the sea.’

In [Avodah Zarah 32a](https://www.sefaria.org/Avodah_Zarah.32a.6), Rabban Shimon ben Gamliel says in the name of Rabbi Yehoshua ben Kefosai. In [Bekhorot 35b](https://www.sefaria.org/Bekhorot.35b), Rabbi Yehoshua ben Kefosai disagrees with Rabban Shimon ben Gamliel and Rabbi Yose.

In the Tosefta, Demai, chapter 1, halakhah 10, and in the Yerushalmi there, chapter 3, halakhah 4, Rabbi Yehoshua ben Kofsai (in the Yerushalmi the reading is Kabsoy) says: ‘All my days I read this verse—and I found it only in the treasury of Yavneh.’ In Bekhorot 39a there is a dispute between Rabbi Yehoshua ben Kefutzai and Rabbi Hanina ben Antigonus.[^4][^6]

Rabbi Akiva saw that there was blessing in him and gave him his daughter as a wife. He lived long, until the time of Rabbi, as in Shabbat 146a (Hyman’s printed citation): Yehoshua ben Kefosai, the son-in-law of Rabbi Akiva, said before him: ‘Rabbi, did Rabbi Akiva not impose liability for a sin-offering in this case?’ He replied: ‘Was Rabbi Akiva particular to this extent?’ Rabbi let down his cloak.[^1][^2]

In [Yerushalmi Pesachim, chapter 6, halakhah 1](https://www.sefaria.org/Jerusalem_Talmud_Pesachim.6.1.7), Rabbi Yoshia ben Kabsa said: ‘All my days I fled from authority. Now that I have entered it, anyone who comes and removes me—with this kettle I will come down on him.’[^1][^3][^5]
Something similar is said in Menachot 109b about Rabbi Yehoshua ben Perachya.

notes.text: Hyman cites Shabbat 146a; the corresponding account is Shabbat 147a:10. His Pesachim citation, chapter 6, halakhah 1, folio 36a, corresponds to the passage linked here as Jerusalem Talmud Pesachim 6:1:7.
“To this extent” expands עד כאן; both the question about sin-offering liability and the reply are rhetorical questions.

Hyman gives the forms Kabsa, Kabsoy, Kofsai, Kefutzai and, in his citation of Zuckermandel’s Tosefta, Kevusai. In the final Pesachim account he writes Yoshia; the corresponding Yerushalmi passage has Yehoshua ben Kabusai.
Hyman abbreviates the treasury-of-Yavneh saying without quoting the verse. The fuller Tosefta and Yerushalmi accounts quote “the pure shall sprinkle upon the impure” (Numbers 19:19).
The kettle is a threatening image: the Yerushalmi continues that it scalds, wounds and burns. Hyman has “with this kettle”; the Yerushalmi has “like this kettle.”
Hyman cites Tosefta Demai 1:10; the treasury-of-Yavneh saying is numbered 1:14 in Lieberman’s edition.
